correlate.executive_summary: Automated reconnaissance and port scanning identified a public web service (nginx on 80/443) hosting a WordPress site. Several application-era artifacts and sensitive paths (/.env, /.git/*, /phpinfo.php) appear present (server returned 403 responses that differ from a baseline 404), indicating discovery of resources that could be risky if access controls change. The WordPress login page (/wp-login.php) is reachable (HTTP 200) and standard security headers are missing or permissive (no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy; CSP allows frame-ancestors *). A filtering layer or request blocking behavior was observed (403s to many user agents), which may impact testing and user experience but also indicates some request inspection in place.

findings.title: Discoverable environment files (.env, .env.example) detected (responses differ from baseline)
findings.evidence: recon: HTTP 403 on /.env and /.env.example (differs from baseline 404 response); body sha256=c029d1c560ecb35b... (recon discovery entries).

findings.title: Discoverable .git repository paths detected (.git/config, .git/HEAD) — existence confirmed by differing response
findings.evidence: recon: HTTP 403 on /.git/config and /.git/HEAD (differs from baseline 404 response); body sha256=c029d1c560ecb35b... (recon discovery entries).

findings.title: phpinfo.php route exists (server indicates presence but access blocked)
findings.evidence: recon: HTTP 403 on /phpinfo.php (differs from baseline 404 response); body sha256=c029d1c560ecb35b... (recon discovery entry).

findings.title: WordPress detected and login page accessible (/wp-login.php)
findings.evidence: recon: HTTP 200 on /wp-login.php (differs from baseline 404 response); body sha256=11e85ef11c4a137a...; recon also observed /wp-admin and /wp-content returning 301 (recon discovery and body matches include 'WordPress').

findings.title: HTTP services detected (nginx) on ports 80 and 443
findings.evidence: nmap: -sV detected http (nginx) on tcp/80 and tcp/443, state=open (nmap service_version entries).

findings.title: Missing or permissive security headers (no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy; CSP frame-ancestors = *)
findings.evidence: recon: Response did not set strict-transport-security, x-content-type-options, x-frame-options, or referrer-policy. nmap http-security-headers: Content-Security-Policy header present with frame-ancestors * (permissive).

findings.title: Request filtering / WAF-like behavior observed (403 for many user agents)
findings.evidence: nmap http-useragent-tester: Status for browser useragent: 403 and list of allowed user agents reported (script output showing multiple user agents listed and 403 results).

findings.title: Technology fingerprint: PHP/8.4.27, Server: hcdn, WordPress (suspected)
findings.evidence: recon: Detected header hints x-powered-by: PHP/8.4.27 and Server: hcdn; body matches include 'WordPress'. Recon marked this fingerprint as suspected.

correlate.deduplication_notes: Multiple recon 'discoverable path' entries describing similar server behavior were grouped: /.env and /.env.example combined into a single environment-files finding; .git/config and .git/HEAD combined into a single .git exposure finding. All individual missing-security-header entries were consolidated into one security-headers finding (including the nmap-observed permissive CSP). Nmap port/service entries for 80 and 443 were combined into a single HTTP services finding. No raw vulnerabilities were invented; CVE lookup for nginx failed and no versioned CVEs could be confirmed, so no findings were upgraded based on CVEs.
